sections.html:
University Place is a mostly suburban Pierce County city on Tacoma's west side, with Puget Sound shoreline. Owned homes here carry a median value of $624,800, and 57.2 percent of households are owners. The population is about 35,479, a 1.7 percent rise since 2020.

Median household income is $99,031, and 19.5 percent of residents are 65 or older. The average commute is 28 minutes. Few households move, since 87.8 percent stayed at the same address over the past year.

The city covers 8.34 square miles at about 417 feet of elevation. Puget Sound lies to the west, Lakewood to the south, and Tacoma to the north and east, with Fircrest along part of the eastern edge. Before August 31, 1995, the area was unincorporated Pierce County.

Locals know the city for Chambers Bay, a links-style course that opened in 2007 and held the 2015 U.S. Open. The 28-acre Town Center holds city hall, a county library branch, the police offices and a public plaza among homes and shops, and Cirque Park hosts community events and youth sports.

The University Place School District serves most of the city, with eight public schools. Primary schools run kindergarten through fourth grade, intermediate schools cover five through seven, junior high is eight and nine, and high school is ten through twelve.

  • Primary: Chambers, Evergreen, Sunset and University Place.
  • Intermediate: Drum and Narrows View.
  • Junior high and high school: Curtis Junior High and Curtis Senior High.

Parts of the city belong to Tacoma Public Schools or the Steilacoom Historical School District. Before you tell a buyer which schools apply, check the district shown on the county parcel record. Charles Wright Academy is also inside the city.

sections.h2: Permits for work on the house
sections.html:
A permit is required to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move or tear down a building, or to change its occupancy. New or replacement electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems also need one. Planning and Development Services handles each request, and you send applications to Permits@Cityofup.com. A buyer's inspector may ask for the permit history of any recent remodel, so having it ready speeds up the review and shows you have nothing to hide.

Ask the department whether any finished job, such as a garage conversion, a new furnace or a water heater swap, still lacks a final inspection. Keep the paper trail so the buyer can see it.

Street projects can also affect showings on your block, so ask the city what work is planned near your address. Raked leaves belong in yard waste bags rather than the street, where they clog storm drains.

sections.h2: Real estate excise tax on a sale
sections.html:
University Place levies its own 0.5 percent excise tax on the sale price, and the Pierce County Treasurer collects it alongside the state tax. Each month the county forwards 99 percent to the city for capital projects and keeps 1 percent to cover collection.

Washington's own portion steps up with price, starting at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and moving to 1.28 percent through $1,525,000. Sales on or after January 1, 2027 use higher thresholds of $551,000 and $1,551,000. You owe the tax when the sale happens, and unpaid tax draws interest after 30 days. The Department of Revenue lists 6 percent as the 2026 interest rate on late excise tax.

A house priced near the $624,800 median crosses the first bracket, which means the total is a blend of rates. Ask a title company to run the exact math. Owners who rent the house out or run a business from it should also ask the city about business and occupation tax, utility tax and its fee schedule.

Call the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer at (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and senior or disability exemptions, or use the treasury line at (253) 798-8678. In January 2027 an expanded state program begins lowering taxes for more Pierce County owners who are 61 or older or who have a qualifying disability.

Ask the office for payoff amounts on any unpaid tax before you accept an offer, since closing has to clear them.

sections.h2: The seller disclosure and the buyer's window
sections.html:
RCW 64.06.020 gives the buyer three business days after receiving the disclosure form to rescind the agreement, unless both sides agree otherwise. If a seller never hands over a completed form, the buyer may waive that right before or after signing the contract.

The clock starts when the buyer receives the form, so handing it over early keeps the schedule predictable. Answer candidly and include any repairs or unpermitted work you know about.

After a buyer signs, several items run in parallel. The disclosure form goes to the buyer, who then has the rescission window described above. Title or escrow orders payoff figures from the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer, and the excise tax is calculated on the final price and paid to the county treasurer at the time of sale.

Before the closing date, collect permit records for any finished work and note any gaps with Planning and Development Services. If a gap turns up, fixing it early costs less than a renegotiation. Ask the closing agent which fees you owe and which the buyer covers, and get that division in writing.

Recording the deed completes the sale. A cash purchase tends to move through these steps faster because no lender adds conditions, although title review still has to finish. Keep copies of everything you sign, and make sure utilities and keys are handled on the agreed day.

sections.h2: Listing or taking a cash offer
sections.html:
List when the house shows well and you can wait out showings and a buyer's loan. Lean toward cash when the house needs work, is part of an estate or must close by a set day.

Compare offers by the money you keep:

  • Take commission, repairs, staging and carrying costs out of the listing price.
  • Learn which side pays excise tax, title and recording costs with each cash buyer.
  • Pin down the closing date and the escrow company.
  • Insist on a written offer that shows when it expires.

For an inherited house, a probate attorney or the Pierce County Superior Court can say what authority is needed before anyone signs a deed.

faqs.q: How many people live in University Place?
faqs.a: The latest estimate is 35,479, compared with 34,866 at the April 2020 count.

faqs.q: What is the real estate excise tax in University Place?
faqs.a: It is 0.5 percent of the price for the city, plus the state's graduated rate that begins at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000. The county treasurer collects both, and the seller owes them at sale.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes on a University Place house?
faqs.a: Call the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer at (253) 798-6111 for values, statements and exemptions. The treasury line is (253) 798-8678.

faqs.q: Which school district serves University Place?
faqs.a: The University Place School District serves most of the city, with eight public schools including Curtis Senior High. Parts of the city fall in Tacoma Public Schools or the Steilacoom Historical School District.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell or fix up a house in University Place?
faqs.a: A permit is required to alter or repair a building or replace plumbing, electrical, gas or mechanical systems. Email Permits@Cityofup.com to ask about records for work already done.
